harvest-session.sh copies files but never runs git add/commit. Harvested files land as untracked in working tree. The hook then rm -rf's the session dir (line 165).

Two destruction paths: Path A (SessionEnd fires, harvest copies but no commit — working tree changes are ephemeral). Path B (SessionEnd never fires — scratch-init.sh deletes dirs >24h old without harvesting). Evidence points to Path B for Z1IhGrcgGO.
Handoff line 9 predicted the problem with scratch path migration note, but assumed SessionEnd hook would fire and succeed. It did not.

Channel infrastructure: decisions #22 (8 components), #34 (13 components), #50 (13 components) — all 'proposed'. Only artifact is one manually created running estimate at wrong path.
/scratch skill lifecycle warning ('Never put carry-forward artifacts in scratch') was added in v0.62.4 (bf21f21) — AFTER most Z1IhGrcgGO scratch files were created.

insights.analysis: Harvest hook has two-phase reliability gap: Phase 1 failure (SessionEnd never fires — files destroyed by stale cleanup). Phase 2 failure (SessionEnd fires, copies but nobody commits — untracked files are ephemeral). Root cause: cp treated as sufficient for persistence, but harvesting/ requires git commit.
Handoff scratch migration note creates false assurance — tells accepting sessions to look at harvesting/ paths, but those paths may be empty if either failure mode triggered.

30 lost files represent the session's primary intellectual output: state audit, findings, investigations, barrier analyses, decision drafts, provenance research, delegation packages, Schwerpunkt assessment. Handoff inlined essential decision content (section D.3) so accepting session can still ACT, but full investigation depth is irrecoverable.

Running estimate is not carrying forward. Only instance is at session-scoped gitignored path, not decision #50's fixed tracked path. No channel-init.sh, no schema, no discovery mechanism for accepting sessions.

Scratch stale-cleanup (rm -rf dirs >24h) is destructive without safeguards. The 24h threshold is reasonable for crash recovery but catastrophic for multi-day gaps between sessions — the 'janitor deletes evidence' pattern.
/handoff skill step 5 verification criterion 2 (reference integrity) would have caught this within the session — but it's a WARNING not PREVENTION. Cannot force the harvest hook to succeed.
